name: Break the Chains
tag: A free 20-chapter guide and practice studio for Merkaba meditation and working through fear.

scenarios.title: Plan your path through the guide
scenarios.ask: I can give {minutes} minutes a day and read {per_week} chapters a week. Plan my path through the 20 chapters.
steps: Guide
Split the 20 chapters into {=ceil(20 / per_week)} weekly sections.
Practice planner
Paired each chapter with a short practice that fits in {minutes}.
Reminders
Set a gentle daily reminder you can snooze or turn off.
Journal
Added a short reflection prompt at the end of each chapter.
followups: The plan simply moves forward from where you are. There is no streak to lose.
Do I need experience with meditation?
No. Early chapters start with simple breathing and posture before the Merkaba visualization.

scenarios.title: Build a practice session
scenarios.ask: Build a {length} session with {breaths} guided breaths and a {focus} focus.
steps: Studio
Opened with {=max(1, round(length * 0.2))} minutes of settling and posture.
Breath guide
Paced {breaths} slow breaths with on-screen timing.
Visualization
Guided the star tetrahedron visualization with a {focus} theme.
Close
Ended with quiet time and a one-line journal prompt.

result.title: Session ready
rows: A reflective practice, not medical or mental health care

followups: In this practice it means picturing two interlocking tetrahedrons, a star shape, around the body while breathing slowly. The guide explains it step by step.
No. It is a reflective practice. If fear or anxiety is affecting your daily life, please talk with a licensed professional.

scenarios.title: Track progress with a fear journal
scenarios.ask: I've written {entries} journal entries over {weeks} weeks. Show what has shifted.
steps: Journal reader
Read your {entries} private entries on your device.
Theme finder
Grouped recurring fears into {=min(6, max(1, round(entries / 5)))} themes.
Trend
Compared how you rated each fear in week 1 and week {weeks}.
Reflection
Wrote a short note with the theme to revisit next.
followups: Only you. Entries stay on your device unless you choose to export them.
They are your own 1 to 10 ratings of how strong a fear felt. They help you notice change over time; they are not a test or a diagnosis.
